title: Underived open-immersion pasting for open base change
statement: Let $k:V\hookrightarrow U$ and $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be composable open immersions. Let $k':V'\hookrightarrow U'$ and $j':U'\hookrightarrow X'$ be their pullbacks along the open-immersion square $U'\xrightarrow{g_U}U$, $X'\xrightarrow{g}X$, and let $g_V:V'\to V$ be the induced map. For a finite commutative ring $\Lambda$ and a $\Lambda$-module sheaf $F$ on $V_{\mathrm{Et}}$, write $b^j_{g,k_!F}$ and $b^k_{g_U,F}$ for the canonical underived maps of [lem-cbc-extension-zero-base-change] for the two open squares, and write $b^{j\circ k}_{g,F}$ for the map for their composite square. If $c:j_!k_!\xrightarrow{\sim}(j\circ k)_!$ and $c':j'_!k'_!\xrightarrow{\sim}(j'\circ k')_!$ are the canonical composition comparisons of [lem-cbc-extension-zero-composition], then, with all inverse-image composition identifications inserted, $$c'_{g_V^{-1}F}\circ j'_!(b^{k}_{g_U,F})\circ b^{j}_{g,k_!F}=b^{j\circ k}_{g,F}\circ g^{-1}(c_F).$$

source.place: Tag 03S6 (lemma-shriek-base-change), with the composition comparison of the extension-by-zero adjunction

proof.text:
Work in sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules on the small étale sites. Write $L_a=a_!$, $R_a=a^{-1}$ for $a=k,j,l=j\circ k$ and their primed versions, and $P_V=g_V^{-1},P_U=g_U^{-1},P_X=g^{-1}$. All the adjunctions $L_a\dashv R_a$ exist by [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction]. Let $r:R_kR_j\xrightarrow{\sim}R_l$ and $r':R_{k'}R_{j'}\xrightarrow{\sim}R_{l'}$ be the inverse-image comparisons. Write $s_k:P_VR_k\to R_{k'}P_U$, $s_j:P_UR_j\to R_{j'}P_X$, and $s_l:P_VR_l\to R_{l'}P_X$ for the cartesian inverse-image identifications. Explicitly $s_j=c_{g,j\prime}^{-1}\circ c_{j,g_U}$ using $jg_U=gj\prime$, and similarly for $s_k,s_l$. The associativity of these comparisons, clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image-composition], gives
$$r'P_X\circ(R_{k'}s_j)\circ(s_kR_j)=s_l\circ(P_Vr).$$
Indeed, both paths reorder $g_V^{-1}k^{-1}j^{-1}$ to $(j'k')^{-1}g^{-1}$ along the two commuting squares. The coherence equation is an equality on abelian sheaves; every arrow lifts to modules by [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition-module-linear], so the same equality holds on modules. No condition on $g$ besides the two cartesian squares is used.

source.place: Tags 0B65 and 0DV0; inverse-image composition from Modules on Sites Tag 03D8 (lemma-push-pull-composition-modules)

proof.text:
Put $t_a=(b^a)^{-1}:L_{a'}P_{\mathrm{source}}\to P_{\mathrm{target}}L_a$. By [lem-cbc-extension-zero-base-change], its transpose under $L_{a'}\dashv R_{a'}$ is $s_{a,L_aM}\circ P_{\mathrm{source}}(\eta_{a,M})$. The mate definition [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] therefore gives, at $G$,
$$t_a^\flat{}_G=R_{a'}P_{\mathrm{target}}(\varepsilon_{a,G})\circ s_{a,L_aR_aG}\circ P_{\mathrm{source}}(\eta_{a,R_aG})
=s_{a,G}\circ P_{\mathrm{source}}(R_a\varepsilon_{a,G}\circ\eta_{a,R_aG})=s_{a,G}.$$
The middle equality is naturality of $s_a$ at $\varepsilon_{a,G}$; the last is the triangle identity. This applies to $k,j,l$, since all three squares are cartesian. Thus $t_k,t_j,t_l$ are exactly the inverse mates of $s_k,s_j,s_l$, respectively.

Use the composite adjunction $L_jL_k\dashv R_kR_j$ of [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. Its unit is $R_k(\eta_{j,L_kM})\circ\eta_{k,M}$. The canonical comparison $c:L_jL_k\to L_l$ is obtained by [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] using the right-adjoint identification $r^{-1}:R_l\to R_kR_j$. In particular its unit equation is
$$(R_kR_j)(c_M)\circ R_k(\eta_{j,L_kM})\circ\eta_{k,M}=r^{-1}_{L_lM}\circ\eta_{l,M}.$$
This is the canonical composition comparison of [lem-cbc-extension-zero-composition], which is the unit-compatible comparison for the restriction models $\rho_a$ of [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction] with the equality $\rho_k\rho_j=\rho_l$ and the transported units $\theta_a\circ\eta_a$. Indeed, put $\theta_k*\theta_j=\rho_k(\theta_j)\circ\theta_kR_j:R_kR_j\to \rho_k\rho_j$. By naturality of $\theta_k*\theta_j$ at $c_M$, the restriction-model unit equation $\rho_k\rho_j(c_M)\circ(\theta_k*\theta_j)_{L_jL_kM}\circ R_k(\eta_{j,L_kM})\circ\eta_{k,M}=\theta_{l,L_lM}\circ\eta_{l,M}$ is equivalent to the displayed equation with $r^{-1}$ replaced by $(\theta_k*\theta_j)^{-1}\circ\theta_l$. That transformation equals $r^{-1}$ by [lem-cbc-open-inverse-image-restriction-composition], so the two comparisons coincide by the uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation]. By the conjugate definition [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate], the equation says $c^c=r^{-1}$: composing with the counit gives this conjugate, and the triangle identity cancels the unit. The identical construction for the primed pair gives $(c')^c=(r')^{-1}$, hence $((c')^{-1})^c=r'$ by the inverse law in that same definition.

Apply clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] with $L_1=L_k$, $L_3=L_j$, $L_2=L_{k'}$, $L_4=L_{j'}$, $G=P_V$, $H=P_U$, $K=P_X$, $\alpha=t_k$, and $\beta=t_j$. The four adjunction hypotheses were verified in Step 1. The pasted square is
$$T=(t_jL_k)\circ(L_{j'}t_k):L_{j'}L_{k'}P_V\to P_XL_jL_k.$$
Step 2 identifies its mate as
$$T^\flat=(R_{k'}s_j)\circ(s_kR_j):P_VR_kR_j\to R_{k'}R_{j'}P_X.$$
This uses composite adjunctions exactly as specified in Step 3; neither comparison $c,c'$ has yet been suppressed.

source.place: mateEquiv_hcomp, line 209; generic adjunction-pasting formula, clause (2) of the cited node

proof.text:
Change from composite extension adjunctions to those of $l,l'$ by forming
$$D=(P_Xc)\circ T\circ((c')^{-1}P_V):L_{l'}P_V\to P_XL_l.$$
Clauses (3a),(3b) of [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] and Step 3 give
$$D^\flat=(r'P_X)\circ T^\flat\circ(P_Vr^{-1})=s_l.$$
The second equality substitutes Step 4 and then cancels $P_Vr$ against $P_Vr^{-1}$ in the coherence equation of Step 1. The mate bijection of [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] is injective. Since $t_l^\flat=s_l$ by Step 2, it follows that $D=t_l$.

source.place: mateEquiv_conjugateEquiv_vcomp, line 486; conjugateEquiv_mateEquiv_vcomp, line 505; mateEquiv bijectivity

proof.text:
All factors of $D$ are isomorphisms, by [lem-cbc-extension-zero-base-change] and [lem-cbc-extension-zero-composition]. Inverting $D=t_l$ at $F$ and using that functors preserve inverses yields
$$b^l_{g,F}=c'_{P_VF}\circ j'_!(b^k_{g_U,F})\circ b^j_{g,k_!F}\circ g^{-1}(c_F^{-1}).$$
Precompose both sides with $g^{-1}(c_F)$; cancellation gives precisely
$$c'_{g_V^{-1}F}\circ j'_!(b^k_{g_U,F})\circ b^j_{g,k_!F}=b^{j\circ k}_{g,F}\circ g^{-1}(c_F).$$
Every inverse-image identification is the module-linear one fixed in Step 1.
